question_text: Define cardiac cycle and cardiac output.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Cardiac cycle
steps.why: The cycle is defined from one beat to the start of the next so that it covers both the working and the resting part of a beat.
common_mistakes: Defining it as one contraction only. It includes the relaxation.
steps.memory_tip: One full beat, start to start, 0.8 seconds.
steps.margin_note: Definition then duration, on two lines.
lines: The cardiac events that occur from the
beginning of one heart beat to the
beginning of the next form the cardiac

steps.label: Cardiac output
steps.why: Output is measured per minute rather than per beat so that it can be compared between a fast and a slow heart.
common_mistakes: Defining output per beat. That is the stroke volume.
steps.memory_tip: Per beat is stroke volume, per minute is cardiac output.
lines: Cardiac output is the volume of blood
pumped out by a ventricle in one minute.

lines.text: It is about 5 litres per minute

insider_note: Both definitions carry a number — about 0.8 seconds and about 5 litres per minute. The complete answer is the definition and its figure, on both halves.
